subtopic: Tensor parallelism / Row-column sharding for MLP and Attention
learningObjective: Explain how tensor parallelism shards MLP and attention weights across devices and what collective is required per layer.
stem: In Megatron-LM-style tensor parallelism with TP degree T, the MLP block up projection W_up is column-parallel (sharded along output dim) and the MLP down projection W_down is row-parallel (sharded along input dim). Which characterization of the resulting dataflow is correct?

options.text: Each of the T devices holds the full [D, F] W_up and computes the full output; only W_down is sharded, requiring one AllGather per MLP block after the activation.

Column-parallel W_up requires an AllGather of x to every device (since each device needs the full input to multiply against its columns); row-parallel W_down then requires an AllGather of the intermediate; two AllGathers per MLP block are needed and TP scaling is bounded by interconnect bandwidth.

The column-then-row parallel arrangement is chosen because it requires no communication at all; the intermediate slices align exactly so that each device's partial down-output equals the correct global output for its shard, so all-to-all is unnecessary.

Column-parallel W_up: each device computes x @ W_up_shard producing 1/T of the intermediate columns; row-parallel W_down: each device multiplies its intermediate slice by its 1/T rows of W_down. A single AllReduce sums partial outputs across devices at the end of each MLP (and separately at the end of each attention block).

explanation: The column-then-row parallel arrangement (Megatron-LM's design) works as follows: (1) The input x is fully replicated on all devices. (2) W_up column-parallel: each device holds F/T columns of W_up and produces 1/T slice of the intermediate. (3) Activation is elementwise, applied per-device. (4) W_down row-parallel: each device holds F/T rows of W_down and multiplies its intermediate slice, yielding a partial output. (5) One AllReduce sums partial outputs across devices. The same pattern applies to attention (QKV column-parallel, output-proj row-parallel with one AllReduce). This is one AllReduce per MLP and one per attention (2 per transformer block).

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: W_up is sharded; the whole point is to shard both to save memory.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: no AllGather is required; the sharded pattern is deliberately designed for a single AllReduce.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: an AllReduce is necessary to sum partial outputs.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: standard Megatron TP pattern with a single AllReduce per MLP.

assumptions: Input x is replicated across TP ranks at the start of each transformer block.
nonImplications: Does not imply TP is always the best parallel strategy; PP and DP have different trade-offs.
Does not imply zero communication overhead; AllReduce cost can be significant.

performanceClaim.scope: Megatron-style TP MLP dataflow and required collective
